newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro laws no problem for Denmark, Jelved says.
newsitem.headline: Euro laws no problem for Denmark, Jelved says.

text.p: Denmark has no problem with the European Commission's proposal on the legal framework for introducing the euro even though it is partly based on Article 235 of the Maastricht treaty, Danish Economy Minister Marianne Jelved said on Monday.
Arriving for Monday's ECOFIN meeting, Jelved was asked whether Denmark would have proplems with the planned legislation.
"Not with the proposal from the Commission," she told Reuters, without giving details. "I handled it in Denmark."

It was the use of article 235 which caused Denmark to threaten to block the EU's countermeasures to the U.S. Helms-Burton legislation. That issue was eventually solved following intense pressure from Denmark's EU partners.
Copenhagen said it would veto the original EU proposal on Helms-Burton because it believed Article 235 compromised national sovereignty.
The Danish government is embroiled in a court case with 11 of its citizens who have complained that Copenhagen is giving away sovereignty.

In the Commission's proposal on the euro, Article 235 is used for legislation concerning the name of the single currency, the 1:1 conversion of the Ecu to the Euro and for the continuity of contracts.
